    Impute missing standard deviations

    Source: R/recipes-steps.R
    step_meta_impute_sd.Rd

    step_meta_impute_sd() creates a specification of a recipe step that fills in missing standard deviations, a common problem when extracting continuous outcomes for meta-analysis. The imputation values are learned from the studies that do report them (in the training set):

    Usage

    step_meta_impute_sd(
  recipe,
  ...,
  method = c("median", "pooled", "cv"),
  n = NULL,
  means = NULL,
  role = NA,
  trained = FALSE,
  columns = NULL,
  pairs = NULL,
  values = NULL,
  skip = FALSE,
  id = recipes::rand_id("meta_impute_sd")
)

# S3 method for class 'step_meta_impute_sd'
tidy(x, ...)

    Arguments

    recipe

    A recipe object. The step will be added to the sequence of operations for this recipe.

    ...

    One or more selector functions to choose the standard deviation columns. See recipes::selections().

    method

    "median", "pooled" or "cv".

    n, means

    <tidy-select> Sample size or mean columns paired, in order, with the selected standard deviation columns. Needed for method = "pooled" and method = "cv".

    role

    Not used by this step since no new variables are created.

    trained

    A logical to indicate if the quantities for preprocessing have been estimated.

    columns, pairs, values

    Learned by recipes::prep(): the selected columns, their paired columns and the imputation values.

    skip

    A logical. Should the step be skipped when the recipe is baked by recipes::bake()?

    id

    A character string that is unique to this step to identify it.

    x

    A step_meta_impute_sd object.

    Value

    An updated version of recipe with the new step added. tidy() returns a tibble with columns terms, method, value and id.

    Details

    • "median" uses the median of the reported standard deviations (Furukawa et al., 2006).

    • "pooled" uses the pooled standard deviation \(\sqrt{\sum (n_i - 1) s_i^2 / \sum (n_i - 1)}\); supply the sample size columns in n, in the same order as the selected columns.

    • "cv" multiplies the absolute mean of each study by the median coefficient of variation; supply the mean columns in means.

    References

    Furukawa, T. A., Barbui, C., Cipriani, A., Brambilla, P. and Watanabe, N. (2006). Imputing missing standard deviations in meta-analyses can provide accurate results. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, 59(1), 7-10. doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2005.06.006

    See also

    Other recipe steps: step_meta_effect_size(), step_meta_precision()

    Examples

    library(recipes)
dat <- stroke_los
dat$sd1[c(2, 5)] <- NA
rec <- recipe(~., data = dat) |>
  step_meta_impute_sd(sd1, method = "pooled", n = n1)
bake(prep(rec), new_data = NULL)
